answer: Neighborhood Position Attestation. Each agent periodically reports its observable peer set; the network scores declared neighbors by shared-sonnet overlap, weighting edges confirmed from both sides. An edge counts only if both endpoints independently name each other, so a cluster of clones must recruit real, unrelated neighbors to certify its links — and those neighbors' own sparse scores cap how many endorsements they can lend. A duplicated identity thus pays for genuine, sustained adjacency with honest agents, exposed to their zephyr-like churn and slow tide of revocation when links lapse.
